- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply downward bias of 5–10% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply smoothing decay (e.g., 80% of previous day’s forecast) for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model exhibits high variance; use moving average of last 5–7 days as baseline for correction.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract mean reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 3–5 days), reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–7 days to avoid lagged overreaction.
